description: Issue #839: a cross-depth duplicate in the NESTED-FIRST orientation. `dup` is declared inside `define outer` on line 2 and again at the top level on line 6, and `params.original_span` names the NESTED one — because "earlier" is a property of source order, not of depth. `spec/execution-model.md:86-87` is explicit that it is "a name an EARLIER declaration in the program already registered" that raises. Its mirror is `nested-duplicate-definition` (top-level first). Both orientations are needed: a two-pass registration that visited every top-level declaration before descending — a plausible "so forward references resolve" refactor — preserves the top-level-first orientation and INVERTS this one, flagging the line-2 declaration as the duplicate and naming line 6 as the original, so the learner stands on the earlier line and is told they already defined it later. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy does not appear beside the check's.
